```js
function slugify(title) {
  return title
    .toLowerCase()
    .trim()
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9\s-]/g, '')
    .replace(/[\s-]+/, '-')
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');
}
```

The bug: `.replace(/[\s-]+/, '-')` is missing the global flag `g`. payload.root_cause: The separator-collapsing regex in slugify (src/text.js:11) lacks the global flag: `.replace(/[\s-]+/, '-')`. JavaScript's String.prototype.replace with a non-global regex replaces only the first match, so only the first whitespace/hyphen run in the title is converted to a dash; all subsequent separators are left untouched. Adding the `g` flag (`/[\s-]+/g`) makes every separator run collapse to a single dash.
